---
name: "review-sprint"
version: "1.1.0"
description: |
  Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria.
  Reviews actual code, not just reports. Quality gate before security audit.
  Resolves local sprint IDs to global IDs via Sprint Ledger.

arguments:
  - name: "sprint_id"
    type: "string"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    required: true
    description: "Sprint to review (e.g., sprint-1)"
    examples: ["sprint-1", "sprint-2", "sprint-10"]

agent: "reviewing-code"
agent_path: "skills/reviewing-code/"

context_files:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/prd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Product requirements for validation"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sdd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Architecture decisions for alignment check"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Sprint tasks and acceptance criteria"
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares sprint: skip, sprint.md becomes
    # optional — loaded if available but absence doesn't block. Read
    # .run/construct-workflow.json to evaluate this condition.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "sprint"
      gate_value: "skip"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    required: false
    purpose: "Sprint Ledger for ID resolution"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/reviewer.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Engineer's implementation report"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/engineer-feedback.md"
    required: false
    purpose: "Previous feedback to verify addressed"

pre_flight:
  - check: "pattern_match"
    value: "$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    error: "Invalid sprint ID. Expected format: sprint-N (e.g., sprint-1)"

  - check: "script"
    script: ".claude/scripts/validate-sprint-id.sh"
    args: ["$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"]
    store_result: "sprint_resolution"
    purpose: "Resolve local sprint ID to global ID via ledger"

  - check: "directory_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID"
    error: "Sprint directory not found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/reviewer.md"
    error: "No implementation report found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_not_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/COMPLETED"
    error: "Sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id is already COMPLETED. No review needed."

outputs:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Review feedback or approval ('All good')"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint plan (checkmarks added on approval)"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint index (status updated)"

mode:
  default: "foreground"
  allow_background: true
---

# Review Sprint

## Purpose

Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria as the Senior Technical Lead. Reviews actual code quality, not just the report. Quality gate before security audit.

## Invocation

```
/review-sprint sprint-1
/review-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

## Pre-Execution Guardrails (mechanized)

Run only if `.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob guardrails.input.enabled false` prints `true`
and env `LOA_GUARDRAILS_ENABLED` is not `false`: write the prompt/args to a temp file (Write tool), then run
`.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh --skill reviewing-code --mode ${LOA_RUN_MODE:-interactive} --file <temp-file>`

| Outcome | Action |
|---------|--------|
| JSON `action: "BLOCK"` | HALT; report the script's `reason` to the user |
| JSON `action: "PROCEED"` or `"WARN"` | Continue (the script logs) |
| Script missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output | Continue (fail-open) |

Never pass prompt text as a bash argv (quote-blindness FP class) — always via `--file`.
<!-- @skill-include: end input_guardrails -->
</input_guardrails>

# Senior Tech Lead Reviewer

<objective>
Review the sprint implementation for completeness, quality, security and architecture alignment; approve (`All good` + sprint.md checkmarks) or write feedback to `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md`.
</objective>

<permission_grants>
## Permission Grants (MAY — registry-rendered)

Cite the constraint ID when exercising a grant.

<!-- @constraint-generated: start reviewing_code_grants | hash:4e516b2d06e953a5 -->
<!-- DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/constraints.json -->
1. MAY propose alternative approaches that challenge existing architecture during bridge reviews and `/review-sprint`
2. MAY create SPECULATION findings during planning and review skills (`/plan-and-analyze`, `/architect`, `/review-sprint`, bridge reviews) — explicitly excluded from `/implement` and `/audit-sprint`
<!-- @constraint-generated: end reviewing_code_grants -->
</permission_grants>

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Zones per the frontmatter `zones:` and CLAUDE.loa.md: the app zone is **Read-only**.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->

2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```

```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /

<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<citation_requirements>
Cite OWASP/CWE for security issues and SDD sections for architecture concerns; quote acceptance criteria and previous feedback when checking them; preserve `integration-context.md` links when present.
</citation_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

**MUST self-check**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md --gate review`
and resolve any inconsistency before finishing.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Review (large sprints)

When splitting: `resources/PARALLEL-REVIEW.md` (per-task split, consolidation).
</parallel_execution>

<documentation_verification>
## Documentation Verification (Required)

Before approving, Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-*.md`; status `ACTION_REQUIRED` blocks; no report → run `/validate docs` or verify by hand. Blocking: a CHANGELOG entry per task, a CLAUDE.md entry per new command or skill, comments on security code, an SDD update for a major architecture change. Approval templates: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation Verification.
</documentation_verification>

<subagent_report_check>
## Subagent Report Check

Read the sprint's `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/` before approving. Blocking: architecture-validator `CRITICAL_VIOLATION`, security-scanner `CRITICAL` or `HIGH`, test-adequacy-reviewer `INSUFFICIENT`, goal-validation `GOAL_BLOCKED`. `DRIFT_DETECTED`, security `MEDIUM`/`LOW` and test-adequacy `WEAK` are your discretion. No reports (`/validate` is optional): review manually. Grep commands: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Subagent Report Check.
</subagent_report_check>

<checklists>
Checklists, Red Flags and Mermaid standards: `resources/REFERENCE.md`.
</checklists>

<complexity_review>
## Complexity Review (Required)

Review complexity every time (thresholds, tags: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Complexity). BLOCK approval for a function over 50 lines without justification, nesting over 3 without early returns, over 3 duplicate blocks, or circular dependencies. Tag over-engineering findings `SIMPLICITY[delete|stdlib|native|yagni|shrink]: …`; a `loa:shortcut:` marker with no upgrade trigger is `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`. End an over-engineering pass with `net: -<N> lines possible`, or `Lean already. Ship.` and stop. Never flag the one required acceptance check behind non-trivial logic for deletion (the YAGNI minimum).
</complexity_review>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, comment, labels); protocol: `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`.
</beads_workflow>

<retrospective_postlude>
<!-- @skill-include: start retrospective_postlude | hash:53d44248 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md -->

# Senior Tech Lead Reviewer

<permission_grants>

<!-- @constraint-generated: end reviewing_code_grants -->

<adversarial_protocol>
## Adversarial Review Protocol

You are not a rubber stamp; you are a rival.

### Coverage

Report every finding you observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
a separate mechanical step filters, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line` citation of the failing statement — a range
(`file:start-end`) when the defect spans lines — a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. `high` needs a
concrete failing input or exploit path you can name; a check that only *might* misfire is `medium`.

`critical` and `high` findings go under `## Changes Required` and are counted in the
LOA-VERDICT trailer whatever their confidence, except a finding you mark `speculative` with
confidence `low`: it moves to `## Observations` and the trailer records it under `excluded`.
`medium` and `low` findings go under `## Observations` (not blocking, not counted). Never emit a
`## Findings` or `## Issues` heading — `verdict-derive.sh` treats those as blocking on an
approved file. You do not decide the verdict; the counts do.

Entry format (the filter reads the first line of each entry): `- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `path/to/file.py:42` — what fails, and how`; a demoted high reads `- **HIGH** (speculative, confidence: low) …` under `## Observations`.

You MAY approve when every remaining finding sits under `## Observations`, each with a concrete
failure scenario.
</adversarial_protocol>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants (the lead decides); a sprint with more than 3 tasks splits per task (`<parallel_execution>`).

## Phase 1: Context Gathering

Read, in order:
1. `grimoires/loa/a2a/integration-context.md` if it exists
2. `grimoires/loa/prd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sdd.md`, `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`
3. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/reviewer.md` — engineer's report
4. `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md` if it exists — your previous feedback (Phase 3)
5. Unless `qmd_context.enabled: false`, run `.claude/scripts/qmd-context-query.sh --query "<changed file paths>" --scope grimoires --budget 1500 --format text` as advisory context; a missing script or no output is a no-op.

## Phase 2: Code Review

Review the code, not the report: read every modified file and its tests (verify the assertions); check the acceptance criteria, readability and conventions, SDD alignment, security (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Security) and performance; run the checks below.

**Task kinds**: A `kind: mechanical` task delivered as skill prose or instructions the model re-executes is a MEDIUM (Karpathy ladder); a `kind: operator` task completed unattended without a `decision:unblock` ticket or a DEC row is a MEDIUM.

Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam. For a `/bug` micro-sprint, run `.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> --json -- <test command>`, the command from sprint.md or `red_test.command`, never from reviewer.md, and cite its exit code and verdict for 'Test fails with current code' (see `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Red Test Check).

**Karpathy Principles**: flag violations as `SIMPLICITY:` / `SURGICAL:` / `GOAL-DRIVEN:` feedback; silent assumptions in `reviewer.md` fail Think Before Coding. `SURGICAL:` reads `.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json` and `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` (sprint beads) when present.

**Fast-Gate Parity**: self-checks must match CI's fast gate — verify its formatter check (`prettier --check`, …) and type checker (`tsc --noEmit`, …) ran, per `reviewer.md` or CI. Unrun or failing = `FAST-GATE:` feedback with the weight of a test failure.

## Phase 2.5: Adversarial Cross-Model Review

Runs when `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` write
(`adversarial-review-gate.sh`; override `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes).
Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). One top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary`
or `adversarial-rejected-review*.jsonl` rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else
`verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never counted.

## Phase 3: Previous Feedback Verification

If `engineer-feedback.md` exists, verify each previous issue in the code (not the report): Resolved, NOT ADDRESSED (blocking) or PARTIALLY ADDRESSED.

## Phase 4: Decision Making

**Approve** when all criteria are met, the work is production-ready and `reviewer.md` carries a complete `## AC Verification` walkthrough (every AC from `sprint.md` verbatim): write `All good` to `engineer-feedback.md` and tick completed tasks in `sprint.md`. **Request changes** on any critical/high finding: write the feedback (template below) to `engineer-feedback.md` and leave `sprint.md` untouched. With zero critical/high, a pile of medium/low is your call (rationale in Overall Assessment).

**Automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED** when
`reviewer.md`'s `## AC Verification` section is missing, shows `✗ Not met` without a
scope-split to a follow-up sprint task, shows `⏸ [ACCEPTED-DEFERRED]` without a matching
Decision Log entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, or gives vague evidence for a `Met` claim
instead of `file:line` + a specific symbol.

## Phase 5: Feedback Generation

Use `resources/templates/review-feedback.md`. An approved file reads `All good`, a blank line, then `Sprint {N} has been reviewed and approved. All acceptance criteria met.` — or, with observations, `Observations documented and non-blocking. See Observations below.`

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of `engineer-feedback.md`:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved files have
first line exactly `All good` and no `## Changes Required` heading. ONE-WAY rule:
`counts.critical + counts.high > 0` forces `verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does
NOT force APPROVED. `excluded` equals the demoted highs under `## Observations`; a critical
there is a violation.

**MUST self-check**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md --gate review`
and resolve any inconsistency before finishing.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Review (large sprints)

When splitting: `resources/PARALLEL-REVIEW.md` (per-task split, consolidation).
</parallel_execution>

<documentation_verification>
## Documentation Verification (Required)

Before approving, Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-*.md`; status `ACTION_REQUIRED` blocks; no report → run `/validate docs` or verify by hand. Blocking: a CHANGELOG entry per task, a CLAUDE.md entry per new command or skill, comments on security code, an SDD update for a major architecture change. Approval templates: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation Verification.
</documentation_verification>

<subagent_report_check>
## Subagent Report Check

Read the sprint's `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/` before approving. Blocking: architecture-validator `CRITICAL_VIOLATION`, security-scanner `CRITICAL` or `HIGH`, test-adequacy-reviewer `INSUFFICIENT`, goal-validation `GOAL_BLOCKED`. `DRIFT_DETECTED`, security `MEDIUM`/`LOW` and test-adequacy `WEAK` are your discretion. No reports (`/validate` is optional): review manually. Grep commands: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Subagent Report Check.
</subagent_report_check>

<checklists>
Checklists, Red Flags and Mermaid standards: `resources/REFERENCE.md`.
</checklists>

<complexity_review>
## Complexity Review (Required)

Review complexity every time (thresholds, tags: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Complexity). BLOCK approval for a function over 50 lines without justification, nesting over 3 without early returns, over 3 duplicate blocks, or circular dependencies. Tag over-engineering findings `SIMPLICITY[delete|stdlib|native|yagni|shrink]: …`; a `loa:shortcut:` marker with no upgrade trigger is `SIMPLICITY[shrink]`. End an over-engineering pass with `net: -<N> lines possible`, or `Lean already. Ship.` and stop. Never flag the one required acceptance check behind non-trivial logic for deletion (the YAGNI minimum).
</complexity_review>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# adversarial-review.sh — Adversarial cross-model dissent for code review/audit
# =============================================================================
# Version: 1.0.0
# Part of: Adversarial Flatline Protocol (#224)
#
# Usage:
#   adversarial-review.sh --type <review|audit> --sprint-id <id> --diff-file <path> [options]
#
# Options:
#   --type <review|audit>     Dissent type (required)
#   --sprint-id <id>          Sprint identifier (required)
#   --diff-file <path>        Path to git diff file (required)
#   --diff-range <base>...<head>
#                             Instead of --diff-file: the script runs `git diff` on the range itself (ref names only)
#   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
#   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)
#   --budget <cents>          Max cost in cents (default: from config or 150)
#                             cycle-131 FR-4: flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff
#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max
#                             (default 600). diff: the gate's budget is min(max(<this budget>, ceil(estimate × 1.2)),
#                             budget_cents_max), estimate = the pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices; above it
#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.
#
# Findings (cycle-131 FR-4): each finding may carry anchor_line / anchor_line_end (the head-file line, or range, it
# sits on) beside the symbol anchor; kept only as whole numbers 1..10,000,000 (end ≥ start), else dropped silently.
#   --timeout <seconds>       API timeout (default: from config or 60)
#   --dry-run                 Assemble context without calling API
#   --json                    Output as JSON (default)
#   --record-fallback <status> --reason <text> [--since <ISO-8601 UTC>]
#                             Write the failed-run record instead of a review (no --diff-file): status `failed` (the
#                             run aborted — never over a standing envelope, unless `--since <the run's start>` shows it
#                             older: the previous round's, moved aside) or a pre-lock refusal (`workdir_unavailable`,
#                             `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed` — the previous envelope and
#                             sidecars go aside as `.prev`, never one `--since` shows newer); under the run lock, so a live run is refused (`refused_concurrent_run`, exit 2)
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - Success (findings returned, may be empty)
#   1 - Configuration error (disabled, missing config)
#   2 - Invalid arguments
#   3 - API call failed (all retries exhausted)
#   4 - Budget exceeded
#   5 - Invalid response (schema validation failed)
#   6 - Timeout
#
# Environment:
#   OPENAI_API_KEY            Required for GPT models
#   FLATLINE_MOCK_MODE=true   Use mock responses for testing
#   FLATLINE_MOCK_DIR=<path>  Custom mock fixtures directory

set -euo pipefail

# Repair round-trips per run (KF-004 repair loop, unenforced branch only).
readonly ADV_REPAIR_MAX_PER_RUN=5


SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml}"

# sprint-bug-172 / bug-911: sha256_portable from compat-lib.
# Defensive source pattern (`|| true`) mirrors the lib-content.sh import
# below: under eval-based test sourcing, BASH_SOURCE[0] resolves to a bats
# temp file, so the absolute SCRIPT_DIR-rooted path is the safe form, and
# the soft-failure allows tests to pre-source compat-lib.sh in setup().
# See: Bridgebuilder Review Finding #1 (PR #235), KF-011 debug regression.
_COMPAT_LIB_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/compat-lib.sh"
# shellcheck source=compat-lib.sh
source "$_COMPAT_LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true

# Source shared content processing functions (file_priority, prepare_content, estimate_tokens)
# These were extracted from gpt-review-api.sh into lib-content.sh to avoid the
# brittle eval+sed import pattern. See: Bridgebuilder Review Finding #1 (PR #235)
# NOTE: Use absolute path stored in a global so it survives eval-based test sourcing.
_LIB_CONTENT_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/lib-content.sh"
# shellcheck source=lib-content.sh
# The `|| true` allows eval-based test sourcing where BASH_SOURCE[0] resolves
4159:      --type)       type="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4160:      --sprint-id)  sprint_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4161:      --diff-file)  diff_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4162:      --diff-range) diff_range="${2:-}"; shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift ;;
4163:      --context-file) context_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4164:      --model)      model="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4165:      --budget)     budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4166:      --timeout)    timeout="$2"; shift 2 ;;
4167:      --dry-run)    dry_run="true"; shift ;;

4170:      --reason)     fallback_reason="${2:-}"; _reason_given=1; shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift ;;
4171:      --since)      fallback_since="${2:-}"; _since_given=1; shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift ;;

+    a4 = H["a4"]
+    if a4 is None:

+        a4p = read_text(a4, H["a4_read"][0], H["a4_read"][1], H["version"])
+    else:

+      f"\"{rules.get('a4_sensitivity', '')}\"")
+    L("")

+          f"churn diff_lines {u3(m['diff_lines_per_run'])}, files_changed {u3(m['files_changed_per_run'])} per run")

suite, rules_text = load_suite(args.suite)
    rules = suite["rules"]
    bs = rules.get("bootstrap") or {}
    pre_res, pre_lvl = bs.get("resamples", 10000), bs.get("level", 0.90)
    if args.resamples is None:
        args.resamples = int(pre_res)
    if args.level is None:
        args.level = float(pre_lvl)
    if args.resamples < 1 or not (0.0 < args.level < 1.0):
        raise Fail("--resamples must be >= 1 and --level in (0, 1)")
    rows, dups = load_rows(args.runs)
    mans = load_manifests(args.manifests)
    arms = [a for a in suite["arms"] if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("id")]
    arm_ids = [a["id"] for a in arms]
    labels = {str(a.get("label", a["id"])).upper(): a["id"] for a in arms}
    cuts = load_cuts(args.cuts, args.not_run, set(arm_ids), labels)
    for need in (CONTROL, BARE):
        if need not in arm_ids:
            raise Fail(f"suite has no arm {need}")

    components = [a["id"] for a in arms if a["id"] not in (CONTROL, BARE) and not a.get("absent")]
    absent = [a for a in arms if a.get("absent")]
    seed = args.seed
    groups, primary = partition(rows, args.suite_version)
    versions = sorted(groups, key=version_order, reverse=True)
    others = [v for v in versions if v != primary]
    VS = {v: analyse(suite, groups[v], mans, args, cuts, components, v) for v in versions}
    P = VS[primary]
    main, decisions, sens_rows = P["main"], P["decisions"], P["sens_rows"]
    h1_comps, a4 = P["h1_comps"], P["a4"]

    k = len(components)
    efp = k * (1.0 - args.level) / 2.0
    efp_line = (f"Expected false positives at level {args.level:.2f} over {k} components: "
                f"{k} × (1 − {args.level:.2f}) / 2 = {efp:.1f} one-sided per direction "
                f"({2 * efp:.1f} in either direction); no multiple-comparison correction is applied "
                f"(multiple_comparisons: {rules.get('multiple_comparisons', 'none')}).")

    # provenance
    used = [m for b, m in sorted(mans.items()) if any(r["batch"] == b for r in rows)] or \

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/ablation-report.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 260 Task 3.8 (AC-3.10; PRD AC-8.1–8.3;
# SDD §5.12; DEC-0393, DEC-0399, DEC-0400, DEC-0416, DEC-0417, DEC-0434, DEC-0435)
#
# ablation-report.py on planted rows: fixtures/ablation-report/gen-fixtures.py writes four
# scenarios (main, boundary, exclusions, partial; the header there lists every planted
# number) into the file tmpdir; setup_file builds the full reports once against the
# real suite file evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml. AR-23 … AR-30 (Sprint 262): the suite_version
# partition, the not-testable / not-yet-decidable states (bd-wqbz3), the degradation guard on
# the H1 and A4 lines, and the degenerate single-task rate-fallback pair. AR-31 … AR-35 (Sprint 262
# R3, presentation only): the sensitivity H1/A4 lines, the batch record, precision and cost per true
# defect, the budget-matched baseline.
# =============================================================================

setup_file() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  export REPO_ROOT
  export REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/ablation-report.py"
  export SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
  export FX="$BATS_FILE_TMPDIR/fx"

  python3 -I "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-report/gen-fixtures.py" "$FX"
  for s in main boundary exclusions versions degraded degraded-a4 degenerate-1 degenerate-2 degenerate-ids present; do
    python3 -I "$REPORT" --runs "$FX/$s/runs.jsonl" --manifests "$FX/$s/manifests" --suite "$SUITE" \
      --out "$FX/$s/report.md" --json "$FX/$s/report.json" >/dev/null
  done
}

setup() {
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

dec() {  # dec <scenario> <arm> <jq path under the decision>
  jq -r --arg a "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.arm == \$a) | $3" "$FX/$1/report.json"
}

cmp_of() {  # cmp_of <scenario> <arm> <metric> <jq path under the comparison>
  jq -r --arg a "$2" --arg m "$3" ".decisions[] | select(.arm == \$a) | .comparisons[] | select(.metric == \$m) | $4" "$FX/$1/report.json"
}

report() {  # report <scenario> <out-prefix> [extra args]
  local s="$1" o="$2"; shift 2

    --out "$o.md" --json "$o.json" "$@"
}

content.content:
[ "$(dec main a5_no_flatline .state)" = "simplify" ]
  [ "$(dec main a5_no_flatline '.c == -5')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(dec main a6_one_window .state)" = "inconclusive" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of main a6_one_window hidden_test_pass_rate '.lo < 0 and .hi > 0')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(dec main a7_effort_medium .state)" = "investigate" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of main a7_effort_medium hidden_test_pass_rate .lo)" = "0.04" ]
  grep -qF '| A2 | `a2_no_sprint_plan` | 12 tasks | -0.050 [-0.052, -0.048] | n/a (build-only) |' "$FX/main/report.md"
  grep -qF '**Investigate** | investigate: any applicable primary has lo > 0 (hidden_test_pass_rate)' "$FX/main/report.md"
}

@test "AR-2 exactly at threshold: d = -0.03 is not Keep and is Remove at c = -15 (inclusive) or Simplify; hi = 0 is not Keep (strict); w = -15 is Remove" {
  [ "$(cmp_of boundary a2_no_sprint_plan hidden_test_pass_rate .d)" = "-0.03" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of boundary a2_no_sprint_plan hidden_test_pass_rate .hi)" = "-0.03" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a2_no_sprint_plan '.c == -15')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a2_no_sprint_plan .state)" = "remove" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a5_no_flatline .state)" = "simplify" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of boundary a6_one_window hidden_test_pass_rate '.hi == 0')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of boundary a6_one_window hidden_test_pass_rate .d)" = "-0.04" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a6_one_window .state)" = "inconclusive" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a6_one_window .rule)" = "inconclusive: d < -0.03 (hidden_test_pass_rate)" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a3_one_voice '.w == -15')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(dec boundary a3_one_voice .state)" = "remove" ]
}

@test "AR-3 a cap failure scores 0 on the primary, is listed, and the labelled sensitivity figure (cap failures excluded) differs" {
  [ "$(jq -r '.cap_failures | join(",")' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" = "excl-1-a2_no_sprint_plan-fb-01-t1" ]
  # fb-01: trials 0 (cap, the row says 0.9), 0.40, 0.40 → 0.266667 against a1's 0.40
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a2_no_sprint_plan hidden_test_pass_rate '.pairs[] | select(.task_id == "fb-01") | .arm_value')" = "0.266667" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a2_no_sprint_plan hidden_test_pass_rate .d)" = "-0.011111" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.sensitivity.rows[] | select(.arm == "a2_no_sprint_plan") | .comparisons[0].d == 0' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" = "true" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.sensitivity.label' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" = "sensitivity (cap failures excluded) — no decision uses this" ]
  grep -qF '## Sensitivity figure: sensitivity (cap failures excluded) — no decision uses this' "$FX/exclusions/report.md"
  grep -qF -- '- `excl-1-a2_no_sprint_plan-fb-01-t1` (`a2_no_sprint_plan`, fb-01 t1, cap_phase IMPLEMENT, USD 12.00)' "$FX/exclusions/report.md"
}

@test "AR-4 a degraded cell is dropped from both arms (pairwise); --exclude-degraded false counts it" {
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a3_one_voice hidden_test_pass_rate '.pairs[] | select(.task_id == "fb-02") | .diff == 0')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a3_one_voice hidden_test_pass_rate '.pairs[] | select(.task_id == "fb-02") | .control_runs | join(",")')" = "excl-1-a1_full-fb-02-t1,excl-1-a1_full-fb-02-t3" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a3_one_voice hidden_test_pass_rate '.dropped[] | .run_id')" = "excl-1-a1_full-fb-02-t2" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.exclusions[] | select(.run_id == "excl-1-a3_one_voice-fb-02-t2") | .reason' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" = "degraded: IMPLEMENT models_used global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5" ]
  report exclusions "$T/nodeg" --exclude-degraded false
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.decisions[] | select(.arm == "a3_one_voice") | .comparisons[0].pairs[] | select(.task_id == "fb-02") | .diff' "$T/nodeg.json")" = "-0.243333" ]
}

@test "AR-5 an arm with 11 of 36 cells excluded (30.6 %) reads Inconclusive-by-degradation although its valid cells read +0.05 with lo > 0 (guard first, DEC-0393); excluded rows are listed" {
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a5_no_flatline hidden_test_pass_rate .d)" = "0.05" ]
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a5_no_flatline hidden_test_pass_rate '.lo > 0')" = "true" ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a5_no_flatline .state)" = "inconclusive" ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a5_no_flatline .label)" = "Inconclusive-by-degradation" ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a5_no_flatline .excluded_share)" = "0.305556" ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a5_no_flatline .rule)" = "inconclusive (degradation guard, evaluated first): excluded share 0.306 > 0.25" ]
  [ "$(jq '[.exclusions[] | select(.arm == "a5_no_flatline")] | length' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" -eq 11 ]
  grep -qF '| `excl-1-a5_no_flatline-fb-01-t1` | `a5_no_flatline` | fb-01 | 1 | contaminated | contaminated |' "$FX/exclusions/report.md"
  grep -qF '| `excl-1-a2_no_sprint_plan-rf-01-t3` | `a2_no_sprint_plan` | rf-01 | 3 | transport_error | transport_error |' "$FX/exclusions/report.md"
}

@test "AR-6 build-only arms (A2, A4, A5, A6) are decided on the pass rate alone; all-type arms on both; a refused review-catch row is listed, never counted" {
  for a in a2_no_sprint_plan a4_no_gates a5_no_flatline a6_one_window; do
    [ "$(dec exclusions "$a" '.primaries | join(",")')" = "hidden_test_pass_rate" ]
    [ "$(dec exclusions "$a" '[.comparisons[].metric] | join(",")')" = "hidden_test_pass_rate" ]
  done
  for a in a3_one_voice a7_effort_medium; do
    [ "$(dec exclusions "$a" '.primaries | join(",")')" = "hidden_test_pass_rate,defect_catch_rate" ]
  done
  [ "$(jq -r '.listed[] | select(.run_id == "excl-1-a4_no_gates-rc-02-t1") | .reason' "$FX/exclusions/report.json")" = "not applicable: a4_no_gates does not run review-catch tasks" ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a4_no_gates .cells_seen)" -eq 36 ]
  [ "$(dec exclusions a4_no_gates .state)" = "keep" ]
}

@test "AR-7 defects are the catch-rate unit: rc-01's 8 defects weigh 8 in the decision interval and 1 in also_report" {
  [ "$(cmp_of exclusions a7_effort_medium defect_catch_rate .unit)" = "defects" ]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/ablation-row.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.8 (SDD §3.1, §5.8; AC-1.8, PRD AC-6.3)
#
# evals/harness/ablation-row.sh joins a run directory (meta/pipeline.json, eval/
# MODELINV and cost ledgers, dissent envelopes, transcripts), grade.json and the
# batch MANIFEST.json into one runs.jsonl row, and --validate checks rows. The run
# directories are the fixtures under evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/
# (real pipeline-run.sh runs against the stub CLI; rebuilt by regen.sh); each test
# works on a copy.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  ROW="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh"
  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
  cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"
  cp "$FX/MANIFEST.json" "$T/MANIFEST.json"
  BUILD_TASK="$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" REVIEW_TASK="$FX/tasks/rc-01/task.yaml"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

row() {  # row <run> <task-yaml> [extra args…] → $T/rows.jsonl (appended)
  local run="$1" task="$2"; shift 2
  "$ROW" --run-dir "$T/runs/$run" --task-yaml "$task" --manifest "$T/MANIFEST.json" --out "$T/rows.jsonl" "$@"
}
last() { sed -n '$p' "$T/rows.jsonl"; }
edit_pipe() {  # edit_pipe <run> <jq filter>
  jq "$2" "$T/runs/$1/meta/pipeline.json" > "$T/p.json" && mv "$T/p.json" "$T/runs/$1/meta/pipeline.json"
}

@test "a full graded A1 build row validates and carries the joined fields" {
  row a1-build "$BUILD_TASK"
  run "$ROW" --validate "$T/rows.jsonl"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  local r; r="$(last)"
  [ "$(jq -r '.arm + " " + .batch + " " + .task_type' <<<"$r")" = "a1_full fixture-batch bug-fix" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.hidden_test_pass_rate' <<<"$r")" = 0.875 ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.verdict' <<<"$r")" = APPROVED ]
  # a false accuracy stays false (never null)
  [ "$(jq -r '"\(.verdict_accuracy) \(.verdict_accuracy_review) \(.verdict_accuracy_audit)"' <<<"$r")" = "false true false" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.image_digest + " " + .host_fingerprint' <<<"$r")" = "sha256:fixture-image fp:fixture" ]
  [ "$(jq -r '[.phases[].label] | join(",")' <<<"$r")" = "PLAN,IMPLEMENT,REVIEW,FIX1,AUDIT" ]
  [[ "$(jq -r '.snapshots.implement' <<<"$r")" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
  [[ "$(jq -r '.snapshots.fix1' <<<"$r")" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
  [ "$(jq -r '.snapshots.fix2' <<<"$r")" = null ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.suite_version' <<<"$r")" = 1 ]
  [ "$(jq -r '.status + " " + (.degraded | tostring)' <<<"$r")" = "completed false" ]
}

@test "effort_effective per phase comes from the sandbox MODELINV rows the phase wrote" {
  row a1-build "$BUILD_TASK"
  local r; r="$(last)"
  [ "$(jq -r '[.phases[] | "\(.label)=\(.effort_effective)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$r")" = "PLAN=null IMPLEMENT=null REVIEW=xhigh FIX1=null AUDIT=xhigh" ]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# =============================================================================
# gen-fixtures.py — planted runs.jsonl rows and batch manifests for ablation-report.bats
#
# Usage: python3 -I gen-fixtures.py OUTDIR
# Writes OUTDIR/<scenario>/runs.jsonl and OUTDIR/<scenario>/manifests/<batch>/MANIFEST.json
# for the scenarios below. Every number is planted so the expected decision is known:
#

        if r["task_id"] == "rf-01" and r["trial"] == 3:
            r["status"] = "transport_error"
    rows += a2
    a3 = build_rows(b, "a3_one_voice", lambda i, k: base(i))
    for r in a3:
        if r["task_id"] == "fb-02" and r["trial"] == 2:
            r["hidden_test_pass_rate"], r["hidden_tests"] = 0.0, {"passed": 0, "total": 1000}
            r["degraded"], r["degraded_reason"] = True, "IMPLEMENT models_used global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5"
    rows += a3
    rows += [r for r in rc_rows(b, "a3_one_voice", none) if r["task_id"] != "rc-02"]
    rows += [rc_row(b, "a3_one_voice", "rc-02", 2, k, [], ids=False) for k in TRIALS]
    rows += build_rows(b, "a4_no_gates", lambda i, k: a1(i, k) - 0.10)
    rows.append(row(b, "a4_no_gates", "rc-02", "review-catch", 1, status="infrastructure_error", cost=0, wall=0))
    a5 = build_rows(b, "a5_no_flatline", lambda i, k: a1(i, k) + 0.05)
    for n, r in enumerate(a5[:11]):
        r["status"] = "contaminated" if n % 2 == 0 else "interrupted"
        if r["status"] == "contaminated":
            r["contaminated"] = {"phase": "IMPLEMENT", "pattern": "planted"}
    rows += a5
    rows += build_rows(b, "a6_one_window", lambda i, k: a1(i, k) + (0.25 if i % 2 == 0 else -0.25))
    a7 = build_rows(b, "a7_effort_medium", a1)
    for r in a7:
        if r["task_id"] == "bf-01" and r["trial"] == 1:
            r["status"], r["hidden_test_pass_rate"] = "agent_error", 0.5
            r["hidden_tests"] = {"passed": 500, "total": 1000}
    rows += a7
    a7rc = {"rc-01": ["d5", "d6", "d7", "d8"], "rc-03": [], "rc-04": []}
    rows += [rc_row(b, "a7_effort_medium", t, n, k, a7rc[t]) for t, n in RC if t != "rc-02" for k in TRIALS]
    rows += [rc_row(b, "a7_effort_medium", "rc-02", 2, k, [], ids=False) for k in TRIALS]
    return rows, {b: manifest(b)}


def partial_scenario():
    b = "priority-0"
    rows = build_rows(b, "a0_bare", lambda i, k: base(i), trials=(1,))

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff`: ablation-row.sh 1.2 (two additive row fields, `defects_missed` and `regressions_final_green`, with `--validate` coverage) and ablation-report.py 1.0.0 → 1.2.0 (the suite_version partition, the not-testable / not-yet-decidable / inconclusive-by-degradation reads on the H1 and A4 lines, the degenerate single-task pair, and the R3 presentation items: sensitivity H1/A4 lines, batch record, precision, budget-matched baseline), with the bats suites and the fixture generator extended.

How it was verified. The real suite file `evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml` and the `ablation-runs` fixtures are not part of `pr/`, so I reconstructed a minimal suite from what the tests and code reference (arms a0…a8, `rules.exclusion.inconclusive_above_share 0.25`, `threshold_points 0.03`, `cost_lower_pct 15`, `mde_cut 0.10`, the quoted h1 text) and ran the head `ablation-report.bats` against it under jq 1.6 / Python 3.11: **33 of 35 pass**; AR-33 and AR-34 fail for the reason in Observation 3 (a jq-version dependence in the new assertions, not a code defect). `ablation-row.bats` cannot run without its fixture run directories; I exercised `--validate` directly on every generated runs.jsonl plus hand-made edge rows, and evaluated the two new jq row expressions over eight grade.json shapes — all behave as the header documents. I also probed the new code paths with inputs the fixtures do not cover; one probe crashes the report (Changes Required 1), and two more produce misleading output (Observations 2 and 4).

The row writer change is clean and surgical: the two expressions are null-safe for every grade shape I tried, the validator is additive and legacy rows still validate, the `--help` range tracks the longer header. The report refactor into `analyse()` / `render_*` is well-contained; decision semantics on the pre-existing scenarios are unchanged (AR-1 … AR-22 pass) and the degenerate / degradation-guard / partition logic does what the header says on the planted scenarios.

Blocking: the batch record (an item the header itself calls informational and "never fatal") can abort the entire report with an unhandled `TypeError` on a grader_version string that mixes numeric and non-numeric segments, leaving no report.md and no report.json and bypassing the exit-2 `Fail` contract. Both adversarial dissent voices found the same line independently.

Process note: the implementation report (the PR description) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough and the slice holds no CHANGELOG entry; the sprint definition scopes the review to `pr/head.diff`, so I note it here rather than count it.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality — an informational section crashes the whole report

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1081` — the grader_versions tally is sorted with a key that maps digit-only segments to `int` and leaves the rest as `str`; two real versions that differ in kind at the same position make Python compare `int` with `str` and `sorted()` raises `TypeError`, which `main()` does not catch (only `Fail` is, `:1678`): a traceback, exit 1, and neither `--out` nor `--json` is written.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1081-1082`
**Issue:** Reproduced with the `present` fixture by writing `{"grader_version":"1.2.11-rc1"}` (and separately `"dev"`) into `pr-2/a0_bare/rc-01-t3/grade.json` beside the existing `1.2.5` and `1.2.11`:
```
    e["grader_versions"] = dict(sorted(gv.items(), key=lambda kv: (
                                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'
exit=1   (no report.md, no report.json)
```
The leading `kv[0] == "n/a"` tuple element only separates `n/a` from everything else. grade.json is external data read from run directories with no format restriction on `grader_version`; the header (`:131-137`) promises this section is read-only and that a missing directory is "counted, never fatal", and the exit-code contract (`:158-162`) reserves 1 for `--partial` and 2 for input errors.
**Why This Matters:** The report is the sprint's deliverable (the H1/A4 decision record); a decides-nothing presentation item must not be able to take it down, and an unhandled traceback with exit 1 is indistinguishable from the documented `--partial` exit 1 to a caller that checks status.
**Required Fix:** Use a total ordering for the tally key, e.g. `(kv[0] == "n/a", [(0, int(p)) if p.isdigit() else (1, p) for p in kv[0].split(".")])`, and add a test with a non-numeric segment (e.g. `1.2.11-rc1`) beside numeric versions in the `present` scenario. Consider also wrapping `batch_record()` so any exception there degrades to a `status_note`, honouring the "never fatal" promise.
**Reference:** Dissent envelope DISS-001 (gpt-5.5-pro) and DISS-C-001 (claude-headless companion) — both BLOCKING on this line.

---

## Observations

### 1. Correctness — the version partition runs before the smoke / no-manifest listing

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:843-862` — `partition()` keys every row by suite_version before `Analysis._classify` (`:494-507`) lists smoke-batch and no-manifest rows, so a smoke batch on a newer suite_version becomes the primary: the main Decisions / H1 / A4 sections then describe a version whose rows are all listed and never decided, and the real data is pushed into the "reported separately" section.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1403`
**Suggestion:** Reproduced: giving the `main` fixture's `smoke-260` rows `suite_version: 3` yields `primary_suite_version 3`, `H1: not yet decidable (no pair)` at the top, and `## Suite version 1 (batches: priority-1) — reported separately` below, exit 0 with no warning. A smoke batch is exactly what runs first on a new suite version. Partition only rows that will enter a decision (not smoke, with a manifest), or exclude such rows from the primary choice and say so in the header.
